editorial.headline: Radioactive Materials and Ionising Generators, Clearly Defined
editorial.standfirst: An open PMA activity for wholesale trade and specified imports of radioactive materials and ionising-radiation generators, available at every listed business scale.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade in radioactive materials and ionising radiation generators is a tightly stated commercial activity. It covers the wholesale trade of radioactive substances and ionising-radiation generators, while its scope expressly includes the import of ionising-radiation generators and the import of radioactive substances. Those import lines are part of the record itself, not an extrapolation from the word “wholesale”. The result is a registration category with a defined commercial focus: the stated trading and import activity in those named materials and generators.

The business that registers here is the undertaking carrying on that stated wholesale trade, including the specified import lines. It is open at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—so the category is available across the full listed range of enterprise sizes. There is no scale singled out as the only route into the activity. For founders, that means the scale selection is broad while the commercial activity remains specific: wholesale trade in radioactive substances and ionising-radiation generators, with both import activities expressly included.

At national level, the foreign-investment reading is direct. The PMA status is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record places no national ceiling below full foreign ownership for this activity. The 100% ceiling matters because it is expressly stated for this particular registration category and its stated scope. Foreign capital can therefore enter under the national position presented here, at any of the listed scales.

Bali does not overturn that national position. The provincial assessment is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and the activity is not blocked by Bali's moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High. The moratorium described in the record permanently blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island; this activity lies outside that blocked band. The honest Bali conclusion is clean: a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today. The record’s reasoning is risk-based, with no separate Bali ownership ceiling or partnership condition stated.
